hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To help you through this, I need to learn about your children first.

**Please tell me about the child or children you're claiming for:**

1. What are their names?
2. How old are they (or what are their dates of birth)?

This will help me determine which eligibility rules apply to your situation. Child Benefit has different requirements depending on the child's age:
- **Under 16**: Different rules apply
- **16-19 years old**: Need to check if they're in education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible

Please provide me with these details and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm interested in finding out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who is 14 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have one child, **Alex, who is 14 years old**. Since Alex is under 16, this is good news - they meet the basic age requirement for Child Benefit eligibility.

Now I need to check a few more things about Alex's circumstances. Let me ask you the next question:

**Is Alex working full-time?**

By "full-time," I mean working 24 hours or more per week in paid employment.

This is important because even though Alex is under 16, if they're in full-time work, it would affect their eligibility for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're only 14, so they're still in school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is in school and not working full-time, which is what we need to see. Let me navigate to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Let me correct that - I need to navigate based on Alex's age category:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good - now I can confirm: **Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

You've already told me Alex doesn't work at all, so the answer is **yes**. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check: **Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

Specifically, I need to know: Is Alex receiving any of these benefits in their own name:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Income Support
- Job Seeker's Allowance

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name. They're just a regular 14-year-old at school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex doesn't receive any of those benefits. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships: **Is Alex currently in an apprenticeship?**

This is important because:
- In **England**: All types of apprenticeships disqualify (Intermediate, Advanced, Higher, Degree Apprenticeships)
- In **Scotland**: Modern Apprenticeships disqualify
- In **Wales**: Foundation Apprenticeships are approved (allowed), but other apprenticeships disqualify
- If Alex is **not in any apprenticeship**, that's perfectly fine for Child Benefit purposes

Since you mentioned Alex is just a regular 14-year-old at school, I assume the answer is no - but please confirm: **Is Alex in any kind of apprenticeship program?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in an apprenticeship. Like I said, they're just 14 and in regular school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex is in regular school, not an apprenticeship. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. This is about **where you (the claimant) live**, not Alex.

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

The main requirement is that you normally live in the UK. However, there are also some special circumstances that can qualify you, such as:
- Having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme
- Being a Crown servant living abroad
- Other specific circumstances related to pre-settled status

For most people, the simple answer is whether they normally live in the UK. Can you confirm: **Do you normally live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm living abroad at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. You're living abroad, which means we need to check if any of the special circumstances apply to you. Let me ask you a few questions to see if you might still qualify:

**Do any of these situations apply to you?**

1. **Are you a Crown servant living abroad?** (This includes diplomats, military personnel, or other Crown employees posted abroad by the UK government)

2. **Do you have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?**

3. **Do you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme?** (If yes, I'll need to ask follow-up questions about your circumstances - such as whether you're working, studying, or have sufficient resources)

Please let me know which, if any, of these apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply to me. I'm just living abroad - I'm not a Crown servant, and I don't have settled or pre-settled status.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand. Based on what you've told me, you don't normally live in the UK and don't fall into any of the special circumstances that would allow you to claim Child Benefit while living abroad.

Unfortunately, this means you don't meet the residency requirements for Child Benefit eligibility. Let me provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Child Benefit Eligibility Assessment Result

**Result: NOT ELIGIBLE**

### Summary

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex, even though Alex meets all the child-related eligibility requirements.

### Why You're Not Eligible

The key issue is the **residency requirement**. Child Benefit can only be claimed by people who normally live in the UK. Since you are currently living abroad and don't fall under any of the special circumstances (Crown servant status, EU Settlement Scheme settled status, or pre-settled status with qualifying circumstances), you don't meet this fundamental requirement.

**Alex's eligibility:**
- ✓ Age 14 (under 16 - qualifies)
- ✓ In full-time education at school
- ✓ Not working full-time
- ✓ Not receiving qualifying benefits
- ✓ Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

**Your eligibility:**
- ✗ Not normally resident in the UK
- ✗ No Crown servant status
- ✗ No EU Settlement Scheme status

### Next Steps

If your circumstances change and you move back to the UK in the future, or if you believe you might qualify under one of the special circumstances (such as Crown servant status or EU Settlement Scheme provisions), you can reapply or contact HMRC for further guidance.

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

Is there anything else I can help you with?
